layout.subtitle: Minimal Stack: Go + Chi + Templ + HTMX
dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.welcome.title: Welcome to the PoC!
dashboard.welcome.body: This is an example of a minimal SaaS application built with:
dashboard.stack.chi: Lightweight HTTP router and middleware routing
dashboard.stack.templ: Type-safe HTML templates compiled in Go
dashboard.stack.htmx: Frontend interactivity without a JS framework
dashboard.stack.json: REST API with the standard library
dashboard.communication.title: Communication Flow
dashboard.communication.body: Click the button below to trigger an HTMX request. The browser will make a GET request to /api/status and receive an HTML fragment generated by Templ, then HTMX will insert it into the DOM without reloading the page.
dashboard.communication.placeholder: Click the button to load the status...
dashboard.rest.title: REST Endpoint (JSON API)
dashboard.rest.body: Try visiting /api/info to see the REST endpoint returning a pure JSON payload generated with the stdlib encoding/json package.
dashboard.loan.title: Cross-Field Validation Demo
dashboard.loan.body: Open the dedicated loan application page to try relational validation with live server-side updates through HTMX.
dashboard.loan.link: Go to the Loan Application demo
dashboard.todo.title: PostgreSQL TODO List
dashboard.todo.body: Create and manage persistent TODO items through pgx, PostgreSQL, HTMX, and Templ.
dashboard.arch.title: Architectural Notes
dashboard.arch.item.1: Templ compiles templates into type-safe Go code during the build
dashboard.arch.item.2: HTMX talks to Go handlers that return HTML fragments
dashboard.arch.item.3: PostgreSQL persistence uses pgx with explicit dependency injection
dashboard.arch.item.4: Chi middleware provides logging and automatic recovery
dashboard.arch.item.5: HTMX responses are always HTML: the server decides whether to render a template or JSON
status.title: Status
status.body: This HTML fragment was rendered on the server with Templ and delivered via HTMX. The component is type-safe: the Go compiler verifies the template during compilation.
